pathway.title: NCR Atleos Corp — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: The business profile is average and the earnings base is steadier than it is growing. Revenue was USD 4,354 million in FY2025 and USD 4,397 million for the twelve months to 2026-09-30, 70.6% of FY2025 revenue was recurring, no customer exceeds 10% of revenue and 55% of revenue is earned outside the United States, which gives lenders visible cash flow, but recurring revenue fell 1.6% in FY2025 and rose only 0.7% in nine months of 2026 while remaining contracted revenue fell to about USD 1.8 billion from USD 2.3 billion at 2026-03-31. Self-Service Banking and Network together are 95.3% of revenue and 97.3% of segment Adjusted EBITDA, so softness in either segment reaches EBITDA directly. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 165; 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; calculation D7; calculation D19; calculation D23

Deleveraging is real and has come from earnings and repayment, not from asset sales or equity. Net debt fell by USD 288 million between 2024-12-31 and 2026-09-30, trailing Adjusted EBITDA rose 8.8% to USD 903 million against FY2025, and Adjusted EBITDA margin widened from 17.6% in FY2023 to 20.5% for the trailing year, so leverage fell while debt was repaid and cash was drawn down; pro forma net debt for the consent fee on the 2029 secured notes is not established. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D3; calculation D6; calculation D21

Part of the margin gain is unlikely to repeat. The issuer's trailing figures include net tariff refunds of unstated size, a USD 31.5 million legal settlement that lifts reported EBITDA, and a first-half benefit from lower vault cash costs, and without the legal settlement net leverage at 2026-09-30 would be 2.69x on reported EBITDA rather than 2.59x; fuel and memory chip costs are elevated and expected to stay so. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D14

Cash conversion is thin, so debt reduction from internal cash flow cannot cover the maturity wall. Free cash flow was USD 200 million in FY2025 and USD 276 million for the trailing year, 24.1% and 30.6% of Adjusted EBITDA, and trailing free cash flow is only 10.8% of gross debt, or 9.2 years of repayment, because interest, taxes, capital spending including software and legacy payments absorb most of EBITDA. Capital intensity is rising with owned ATMs under ATMaaS contracts, to 4.2% of revenue in nine months of 2026 from 3.6% in FY2025. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 105; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 106; calculation D8; calculation D9; calculation D23

Liquidity is adequate for the next two years and the covenant test cannot be assessed here. Liquidity of USD 882 million is USD 311 million of cash and USD 571 million of undrawn revolver, against USD 80 million of principal due in 2026 and USD 93 million in 2027, a cover of 5.1x, and the revolver was undrawn at 2026-09-30; a leverage covenant is stated in the credit agreement but the covenant ratio and compliance are not supplied, so headroom is not calculated. Pro forma net debt and cash for the consent fee are not established. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 168; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 170; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D5

Refinancing is the central test, and the debt market currently supports it. USD 2,619 million of principal, 93.8% of the year-end 2025 total, falls due in 2028 and 2029, when the term loans A and the revolver mature on 2028-10-16, the term loan B on 2029-04-16 and the 2029 secured notes on 2029-04-01; the long-term debt had a fair value of USD 2,684 million against principal of USD 2,575 million at 2026-09-30, 104.2% of principal, and the notes are callable at a premium that steps down each year. Brink's financing and the treatment of the credit facilities at closing are not stated. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 166; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 167; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 169; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 170; 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation D4; calculation D15

Rate and cost sensitivity is material to a business with this cash conversion. The issuer estimates that a 100 bp rise in variable rates would add USD 17 million to interest expense and USD 39 million to vault cash rental cost at FY2025 volumes, USD 56 million in all, which is 6.7% of Adjusted EBITDA and 20.3% of trailing free cash flow, and the interest rate swaps on the term loans were terminated on 2025-02-18; fixed-rate notes are 52.4% of principal. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 118; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 119; 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation D16; calculation D17

Financial policy and governance are supportive in conduct and uncertain in outcome. There is no sponsor and no common dividend, buybacks of USD 43 million were suspended for the merger and debt was repaid, but a revenue-control weakness led to revised statements, Voyix legacy claims have no stated cap, and the Brink's merger, with a USD 145 million termination fee equal to 16.4% of liquidity, will change the owner and may change the debt structure on terms creditors cannot yet see. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation D20

runs.text: The first credit strength is deleveraging from earnings and repayment. Net debt fell by USD 288 million in nine months to 2026-09-30 and net leverage on reported EBITDA fell to 2.59x from 3.50x, which shrinks the amount to be refinanced in 2028 and 2029 and improves the odds that lenders and an acquirer will refinance it; pro forma net debt for the consent fee is not established. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D2; calculation D3

The second strength is liquidity that outlasts the nearest maturities. Cash of USD 311 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 571 million give USD 882 million, 5.1x the USD 173 million of principal due in 2026 and 2027, so debt service does not depend on market access before 2028; pro forma cash for the consent fee is not established. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 170; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D5

The third strength is a recurring, customer-spread revenue base. Recurring revenue was 70.6% of FY2025 revenue, no customer exceeds 10% of revenue and 55% is earned outside the United States, which limits the loss from any one customer or market and gives visibility on a large part of EBITDA. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 165

The fourth strength is margin gain from ATMaaS and software. Adjusted EBITDA margin widened from 17.6% in FY2023 to 20.5% for the trailing year as services and software grew, so more EBITDA is earned on flat revenue, although part of the 2026 gain is not repeatable. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D6

The fifth strength is supportive financial policy with no sponsor. The statements show no common dividend and the USD 200 million repurchase program was suspended after USD 43 million of use, so cash has gone to debt reduction, not to owners. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A)

The first credit weakness is the maturity wall. USD 2,619 million, 93.8% of year-end 2025 principal, falls due in 2028 and 2029, and trailing free cash flow of USD 276 million could repay only a small part by then, so the credit depends on refinancing in a market the sources do not show for 2028. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 170; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D4; calculation D9

The second weakness is a change of control with undisclosed financing. The credit facilities make a change of control an event of default, the noteholders' waiver depends on a consent fee that is not stated, and the USD 145 million termination fee equals 16.4% of liquidity, so the owner and the debt structure may change on terms creditors cannot yet see. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 168; calculation D20

The third weakness is weak revenue momentum. Recurring revenue is flat, remaining contracted revenue fell 21.7% from 2026-03-31 to 2026-09-30, Network managed units fell 4.8% in a year and hardware fell 20% in Q3 2026, so EBITDA gains must come from cost and mix while the volume base is not growing. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation D23; calculation D24

The fourth weakness is thin cash conversion. Free cash flow was 24.1% of Adjusted EBITDA in FY2025 and 30.6% in the trailing year, and capital intensity is rising with owned ATMs, so each dollar of EBITDA gain adds little to debt reduction capacity. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation D8; calculation D23

The fifth weakness is sensitivity to rates and legacy claims. A 100 bp rise in variable rates costs about USD 56 million a year at FY2025 volumes, 6.7% of Adjusted EBITDA, and Voyix legacy indemnities and environmental claims draw cash without a stated cap. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 118; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 119; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation D16

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The pending merger with Brink's is the only transaction that changes who owns the debt. Under the agreement signed on 2026-02-26 Brink's acquires each Atleos share for USD 30.00 in cash plus a fixed fraction of a Brink's share, through a first merger in which Atleos survives as a Brink's subsidiary and an immediate second merger into a Brink's limited liability company; stockholders of both companies approved it on 2026-06-30, and closing is expected in early January 2027 subject to antitrust clearances, other regulatory approvals and money transmitter licenses. Atleos may owe Brink's a termination fee of USD 145 million in certain circumstances and has agreed to run its business in the ordinary course until closing. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 127; 10-Q_2026-03-31_natl-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-03-31_natl-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-Q_2026-03-31_natl-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-Q_2026-06-30_natl-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 10; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_ex-991ncratleosearningsrel.htm.jsonl, page 1

Noteholders have already given up their change-of-control put. On 2026-03-11 holders of the 2029 secured notes consented to a supplemental indenture under which the mergers are not a change of control, so no repurchase offer is required; the waiver becomes operative immediately before the first merger and only if the consent fee is paid, and neither the fee nor its funding is stated. The credit facilities contain a change-of-control event of default, and the sources do not say whether Brink's will repay, amend or assume them, so the post-closing debt stack and pro forma net debt are not established. Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_natl-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 168; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Today's debt was created at the separation and reset twice since. On 2023-09-27 Atleos issued the 2029 secured notes and borrowed under term loan facilities for USD 2,894 million, and with cash on hand paid USD 2,996 million to Voyix, so the debt funded a payment to the former parent rather than operations. The credit agreement was amended on 2024-10-17 to provide Term A-1 of USD 835 million, Term A-2 of USD 300 million, Term B of USD 445 million and a USD 600 million revolver, USD 105 million of Term B was prepaid in Q4 2024 without penalty, and the Term B loans were refinanced at SOFR plus 3.00% on 2025-09-18; the 2029 secured notes are the only notes outstanding, and they are callable from 2026-10-01 at a premium that steps down each year. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_ncr-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 133; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 166; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 167; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 165–166; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 169; calculation B19

Other transactions are small. Atleos spent USD 17 million on a business acquisition in FY2025 and USD 1 million in the first nine months of 2026, raised USD 45 million in FY2025 from sales of property and equipment, primarily sale-leaseback of owned ATM units, divested a non-core business for USD 11 million, received USD 31.5 million from a litigation settlement in Q3 2026 and paid Voyix USD 24 million on 2026-07-17 for its half of the Hoak settlement. The USD 200 million share repurchase program approved on 2025-07-25 was used for USD 28 million in FY2025 and USD 15 million in Q1 2026 and then suspended. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 105; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 125; 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 107; 10-Q_2026-03-31_natl-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-06-30_natl-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 48

fields.value: NCR Atleos Corp (issuer id natl-1974138), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. This module extracts the issuer's statements, debt, liquidity and leverage on one basis (USD millions, carrying-value debt) and logs every definition conflict and gap. It makes no recommendation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: NCR Atleos is deleveraging through earnings growth and debt repayment, with net debt of USD 2,233 million at 2026-09-30, or 2.59x reported and 2.47x issuer-adjusted trailing EBITDA, so lenders face limited near-term refinancing pressure but a heavy 2028 and 2029 maturity wall. Gross debt at carrying value has fallen from USD 2,940 million at 2024-12-31 to USD 2,544 million, while cash fell by USD 145 million to USD 311 million as the revolver was repaid.

fields.value: Gross debt at balance-sheet carrying value fell from USD 2,940 million at 2024-12-31 to USD 2,758 million at 2025-12-31 and USD 2,544 million at 2026-09-30, and net debt fell from USD 2,521 million to USD 2,302 million and USD 2,233 million. Trailing issuer-adjusted EBITDA rose from USD 785 million to USD 830 million and USD 903 million, so adjusted net leverage fell from 3.21x to 2.77x and 2.47x, and on the derived reported EBITDA net leverage fell from 3.50x to 3.13x and 2.59x. The 2026 reduction came from repayment: USD 125 million of net revolver repayment and USD 91 million of term-loan payments in nine months, funded by USD 219 million of operating cash flow and a USD 145 million fall in cash.

The issuer's adjusted figure of USD 830 million is USD 94 million higher, chiefly because it adds back USD 51 million of Voyix indemnification expense and USD 34 million of stock-based compensation, so creditors should treat 2.59x rather than 2.47x as the cautious reading of leverage at 2026-09-30.

fields.value: Operating cash flow was USD 356 million in FY2025 and USD 450 million for the twelve months to 2026-09-30, and free cash flow after capital expenditures and capitalized software was USD 200 million and USD 276 million. Q3 2026 operating cash flow of USD 198 million includes legal settlement proceeds that the issuer's bridge deducts (USD 38 million) and compares with USD 27 million a year earlier, when a USD 117 million swing in restricted settlement cash depressed it, so quarterly operating cash flow moves with settlement timing and one-offs and the trailing figure is the better guide.

Scheduled principal is light until 2028, with USD 80 million due in 2026 and USD 93 million in 2027 on the year-end ladder, then USD 949 million in 2028 when the term loans A and the revolver mature and USD 1,670 million in 2029 including the 2029 secured notes, so refinancing ahead of 2028 is the central test.

fields.value: The pending merger with Brink's, expected to close in early January 2027, does not trigger a change-of-control put on the 2029 secured notes because holders consented in March 2026, but the consent fee, the acquirer's financing and the treatment of the credit facilities at closing are not stated, so pro forma net debt is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case against the improving trend is that it leans on adjusted EBITDA and on cash. The derived EBITDA gives 2.59x, the issuer's FY2025 add-backs include USD 34 million of stock-based compensation, a recurring cost, and USD 51 million of Voyix indemnification, cash fell by USD 145 million, and Q3 operating cash flow includes legal settlement proceeds. The trailing derived EBITDA also includes a USD 31.5 million legal settlement gain booked in Q3 2026, and without it net leverage at 2026-09-30 would be 2.69x. Self-Service Banking hardware revenue fell from USD 235 million in Q3 2025 to USD 188 million in Q3 2026, so EBITDA could stall before the 2028 wall if hardware and crypto-related volumes keep falling.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash interest paid is not disclosed in the quarterly reports, so EBITDA cover for 2025-09-30 and 2026-09-30 is not calculable and every interest cover cell for those dates is not supplied, which restricts any 2026 coverage conclusion; Severity Medium; the actions that would close it are an issuer disclosure of cash interest paid for the periods.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The debt maturity ladder is printed only at 2025-12-31 and the 2026-09-30 report gives total principal of USD 2,575 million without a ladder, so principal repaid in 2026 is not scheduled and the maturity wall at the latest date is not established; Severity Medium; a ladder at 2026-09-30 or the tranche balances would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No source states lien priority between the credit facilities and the 2029 secured notes and no intercreditor terms are supplied, so the debt stack shows equal rank as Analyst Judgement and the equipment loan is left out because its rank is not stated; Severity Medium; the credit agreement, the indenture and any intercreditor agreement would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The consent fee on the 2029 secured notes is not stated and the treatment of the credit facilities at the merger closing is not stated, so pro forma net debt and pro forma net leverage are not established; Severity Medium; the merger agreement and the joint proxy statement would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The issuer states no unadjusted EBITDA, so EBITDA is derived from net income, income tax, interest and cash-flow depreciation and amortization, which differs from the issuer's reconciliation by USD 14 million of depreciation and amortization in FY2025; the Q3 quarters use depreciation and amortization derived as nine months less six months, and reported EBITDA is not calculable for the trailing year at 2025-09-30 because nine months of 2024 are not in the sources; Severity Low; an issuer statement of unadjusted EBITDA would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The Q3 2025 balance sheet and the revolver position at 2025-09-30 are not in the sources, so the 2025-09-30 debt and cash come from the Q3 2026 release, and the FY2023 balance sheet is printed only in the original FY2024 annual report before the revision, so FY2023 has no leverage; lines printed in the annual report but not in the quarterly reports are not supplied for the nine-month columns, dashes in the statements are read as not supplied and not as zero, and FY2023 cash interest is external interest only; Severity Low; the earlier quarterly reports would close the first three.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Tranche balances of the term loans at 2026-09-30 and instrument-level carrying values are not disclosed, and the average vault cash balance for 2026 is not stated, so only an aggregate financing cost adjustment of USD 31 million and the FY2025 average of about USD 4.1 billion are shown, and no separate statements for the subsidiary guarantors, the receivables subsidiaries or the acquirer are supplied; Severity Low; a debt schedule, the vault cash disclosure and those statements would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Printed figures disagree in three places: the FY2025 maturity table totals USD 2,792 million against principal of USD 2,798 million, the Q3 2026 release deducts USD 38 million for legal settlements against net proceeds of USD 31.5 million in the quarterly report, and the free cash flow definition is worded differently between the FY2025 annual report and the 2026 releases; all figures are shown with their roles and none is forced to agree; Severity Low; issuer explanations would close them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The FY2024 annual report supplied is the original and was later revised in a Form 10-K/A that is not supplied; FY2024 and FY2023 figures are taken from the FY2025 annual report, which is a resolved conflict for those years, and revised FY2022 figures exist nowhere in the sources; Severity Low and resolved by using the later filing.

fields.value: - The Q1 2026 release prints quarterly net income of USD 22 million and Adjusted EBITDA of USD 172 million beside a net leverage ratio of 2.83x, which implies trailing Adjusted EBITDA of about USD 830 million; the trailing figure was rebuilt from FY2025 plus Q1 2026 less Q1 2025 and agrees; Severity Low and resolved by recomputation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: NCR Atleos Corp (issuer id natl-1974138), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. This module sets out the transaction, ownership, governance, business and operating facts a creditor needs, from the eight supplied filings and earnings releases and the Source readiness answer. It makes no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: NCR Atleos is a publicly listed, mostly recurring-revenue ATM technology and network business with no sponsor or controlling shareholder disclosed, so creditors face event risk from the pending Brink's takeover more than sponsor-extraction risk. Recurring streams were 70.6% of FY2025 revenue and no customer exceeds 10% of revenue, but recurring revenue fell by USD 49 million in FY2025, rose only 0.7% in the first nine months of 2026 and contracted backlog has fallen to about USD 1.8 billion, so the earnings gain comes from margin and mix rather than growth in the recurring base.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 164; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 165; 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; Source readiness (CP-0); calculation B1; calculation B3; calculation B5; calculation B32

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Brink's will pay USD 30.00 in cash plus Brink's shares for each Atleos share, and the 2029 secured notes carry no change-of-control put because holders consented in March 2026, but the credit facilities treat a change of control as an event of default and the sources do not state how they are handled at closing or what the consent fee is.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership carries no sponsor risk but is about to change hands. NCR Voyix distributed all Atleos shares to its stockholders in October 2023 and holds none, no sponsor, fund or controlling shareholder is disclosed, and holder percentages and director holdings are not supplied. Brink's will own Atleos outright once the two-step merger closes, expected in early January 2027, so the owner whose behavior matters to creditors will soon be an acquirer whose financing the documents do not describe.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 127; 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_ex-991ncratleosearningsrel.htm.jsonl, page 1; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings are concentrated in two segments and no customer is large enough to matter on its own. Self-Service Banking supplied 66.2% of FY2025 revenue and 65.8% of segment Adjusted EBITDA, Network supplied 29.1% of revenue and 31.5% of segment Adjusted EBITDA, and Telecommunications & Technology supplied 2.7%, so only the first two matter to credit. No customer exceeds 10% of revenue or receivables, but renewal rates and churn are not supplied, so durability rests on the contracted backlog and segment trends.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 100; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 159; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 165; calculation B7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The recurring-revenue story is a margin story, not a growth story. Recurring revenue was USD 3,075 million in FY2025 against USD 3,124 million in FY2024, a fall of 1.6%, and USD 2,312 million in the first nine months of 2026 against USD 2,296 million, a rise of 0.7%. The Self-Service Banking recurring share of 58% against 61% implies that recurring revenue outside that segment fell by about USD 82 million in FY2025, which fits the 2% fall in Network transaction revenue and the USD 102 million fall in Other revenue as Voyix agreements wind down. In Q3 2026 the recurring share rose to 71.2% from 69.8% only because total revenue fell while recurring revenue stayed at USD 782 million against USD 783 million, and Self-Service Banking annualized recurring revenue grew only 1.8%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 164; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 103; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 100; 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation B3; calculation B4; calculation B5; calculation B6; calculation B25; calculation B26; calculation B30; calculation B34

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: ATMaaS is the growth engine but is still small, and contracted backlog and the Network fleet are shrinking. ATMaaS revenue was USD 258 million in FY2025, up 33.0% and 9.0% of Self-Service Banking revenue, and USD 83 million in Q3 2026, up 23.9% and 11.4% of that revenue. That growth sits inside services and software, whose combined USD 34 million rise in Q3 2026 did not offset a USD 47 million fall in hardware. Remaining performance obligations fell to about USD 1.8 billion at 2026-09-30 from about USD 2.3 billion at 2026-03-31, USD 2.2 billion at 2025-12-31 and USD 2.0 billion at 2024-12-31, with about 75% due within a year, and Network managed units fell 4.8% in a year, so contracted revenue has stopped growing and the Network fleet is smaller than a year ago.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 97; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 135; 10-K_2024-12-31_ncr-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 142; 10-Q_2026-03-31_natl-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-06-30_natl-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; calculation B29; calculation B31; calculation B32; calculation B33

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margin expansion in Self-Service Banking is real and is carrying the earnings. Segment Adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 26.1% in FY2025 from 23.4% as ATMaaS revenue grew 33% and software revenue 14%, and in the first nine months of 2026 segment Adjusted EBITDA reached USD 885 million against USD 826 million, up 7.1%, while unallocated corporate costs fell to USD 220 million from USD 233 million, lifting consolidated Adjusted EBITDA by 12.3%. Part of the 2026 gain is not repeatable, because Self-Service Banking earnings include net tariff refunds whose amount is not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 103; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 159; 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; calculation B8; calculation B9; calculation B11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Hardware and slowing revenue are the swing factors. Hardware was USD 861 million in FY2025, 29.9% of segment revenue and up 14% on the industry refresh cycle, but it fell 20% in Q3 2026 and 7% in nine months, and consolidated revenue growth slowed from 7% in Q1 to flat in Q2 and a 2% fall in Q3. Management attributes part of the weakness to customers delaying purchases in anticipation of the combined company's offering and to the war in the Middle East, so if buyers wait for the merger, near-term hardware revenue and its margin are the first to give.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 103; 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; EX-99.1_2026-05-06_ex-991ncratleosearningsrel.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_ex-991ncratleosearningsrel.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_ex-991ncratleosearningsrel.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation B13; calculation B14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Network earnings depend on withdrawal and Bitcoin volumes that are soft and on vault cash costs that move with interest rates. Transactions are 97.5% of Network revenue, Network revenue fell 1% in FY2025 and 2% in Q3 2026, and the annual report ties the FY2025 decline to US immigration policy effects on withdrawals and lower Bitcoin volume. Network Adjusted EBITDA fell 11% in FY2025 mainly on higher vault cash cost after hedge gains expired and on lost higher-margin revenue, and the average vault cash balance of about USD 4.1 billion stays outside the statements.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Voyix remains a live claimant on Atleos cash after the separation. Atleos paid USD 24 million on 2026-07-17 as half of the final Hoak settlement against an accrual of up to USD 22 million at 2025-12-31, bears half of Voyix's annual environmental cost above USD 15 million with USD 12 million accrued while Voyix controls the work, and owes Voyix tax indemnities that include an acquisition of Atleos stock. Voyix says the Kalamazoo River cost could be more than double its USD 99 million reserve, and whether the Brink's merger engages the tax indemnity is not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy in the record is creditor-supportive. The statements show no common dividend, Atleos repurchased only USD 28 million of shares in FY2025 and USD 15 million in Q1 2026 before suspending the USD 200 million program in connection with the merger, and gross debt at carrying value fell by USD 396 million, from USD 2,940 million at 2024-12-31 to USD 2,544 million at 2026-09-30. The one large debt-funded transfer to an owner was the separation itself, when USD 2,894 million of new notes and term loans plus cash on hand paid Voyix USD 2,996 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 125; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 126; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 107; 10-Q_2026-03-31_natl-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-06-30_natl-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-K_2024-12-31_ncr-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 133; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B19; calculation B23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reporting quality is a governance blemish that has been repaired for now. A material weakness in controls over subscription software revenue led to revised FY2022 to FY2024 statements in a Form 10-K/A filed on 2025-11-05 and to revised Q1 and Q2 2025 figures in 2026 reports; management rates internal control effective at 2025-12-31 and the auditor audited that assessment, so the record of clean reporting under the new controls is short, and Atleos gives no call or outlook while the merger is pending.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 205; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 206; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 209; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_ex-991ncratleosearningsrel.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_ex-991ncratleosearningsrel.htm.jsonl, page 3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Brink's merger is the dominant credit event and the sources describe only its equity side. Holders receive USD 30.00 in cash plus Brink's shares, so Brink's must find at least USD 2,218 million of cash for the basic shares before refinancing any Atleos debt, and the USD 145 million termination fee is 16.4% of liquidity of USD 882 million. Brink's is also a named competitor, so antitrust clearances and money transmitter licenses are closing conditions, and the target date has moved from the end of Q1 2027 in May to early January 2027 in November.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-03-31_natl-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-03-31_natl-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-Q_2026-03-31_natl-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; EX-99.1_2026-05-06_ex-991ncratleosearningsrel.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_ex-991ncratleosearningsrel.htm.jsonl, page 1; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B17; calculation B18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case against a low sponsor-risk, event-led view is that the debt was created by a debt-funded USD 2,996 million payment to the former owner, that the next owner is an acquirer whose leverage is unknown, and that the contracts that protect creditors are not in the sources: the credit facilities make a change of control an event of default, noteholders gave up their put for a fee that is not stated, and no document says how the facilities are treated at closing. The earnings improvement is also thinner than it looks, because recurring revenue is flat, contracted backlog has fallen for two quarters, hardware is falling, 2026 margins include tariff refunds of unstated size, and a legal recovery of USD 31.5 million sits in reported earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_ncr-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 133; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 168; 10-Q_2026-03-31_natl-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; calculation B5; calculation B32

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Disclosure of Brink's financing that repays the credit facilities at closing, or confirmation that the tax indemnity does not apply, would lower event risk, as would a proxy statement that shows no large holder with blocking rights. Brink's financing that leaves Atleos creditors behind new secured debt, a revolver draw to pay the consent fee or termination fee, a tax indemnity that the merger engages, or a further decline in hardware and Network volumes would raise it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The 2026 proxy statement, which carries the board, committee roles, executive pay and holders of more than 5% of shares, is not supplied, so the finding that no shareholder controls Atleos rests on the absence of disclosure rather than a holder table and would change if a large holder exists.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The merger agreement, the joint proxy statement and the financing documents of Brink's are not supplied, so the post-closing owner, its financing and the treatment of the credit facilities cannot be tested and the event-risk finding will move once they are read.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The separation, tax matters and commercial agreements with Voyix are known only through summaries, so whether the merger engages the tax indemnity and how much Voyix business sits inside other revenue and cost lines are not established, which bounds the finding on legacy claims.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Customer renewal rates and churn, the split of contracted backlog by segment, ATM counts by ownership model and the size of 2026 tariff refunds are not disclosed, so the durability of recurring revenue and the quality of the 2026 margin gain are judged from the aggregate backlog and segment trends alone.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The pending merger with Brink's is the only transaction that changes who owns the debt. Under the agreement signed on 2026-02-26 Brink's acquires each Atleos share for USD 30.00 in cash plus a fixed fraction of a Brink's share, through a first merger in which Atleos survives as a Brink's subsidiary and an immediate second merger into a Brink's limited liability company; stockholders of both companies approved it on 2026-06-30, and closing is expected in early January 2027 subject to antitrust clearances, other regulatory approvals and money transmitter licenses. Atleos may owe Brink's a termination fee of USD 145 million in certain circumstances and has agreed to run its business in the ordinary course until closing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 127; 10-Q_2026-03-31_natl-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-03-31_natl-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-Q_2026-03-31_natl-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-Q_2026-06-30_natl-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 10; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_ex-991ncratleosearningsrel.htm.jsonl, page 1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Noteholders have already given up their change-of-control put. On 2026-03-11 holders of the 2029 secured notes consented to a supplemental indenture under which the mergers are not a change of control, so no repurchase offer is required; the waiver becomes operative immediately before the first merger and only if the consent fee is paid, and neither the fee nor its funding is stated. The credit facilities contain a change-of-control event of default, and the sources do not say whether Brink's will repay, amend or assume them, so the post-closing debt stack and pro forma net debt are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_natl-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 168; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Today's debt was created at the separation and reset twice since. On 2023-09-27 Atleos issued the 2029 secured notes and borrowed under term loan facilities for USD 2,894 million, and with cash on hand paid USD 2,996 million to Voyix, so the debt funded a payment to the former parent rather than operations. The credit agreement was amended on 2024-10-17 to provide Term A-1 of USD 835 million, Term A-2 of USD 300 million, Term B of USD 445 million and a USD 600 million revolver, USD 105 million of Term B was prepaid in Q4 2024 without penalty, and the Term B loans were refinanced at SOFR plus 3.00% on 2025-09-18; the 2029 secured notes are the only notes outstanding, and they are callable from 2026-10-01 at a premium that steps down each year.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Other transactions are small. Atleos spent USD 17 million on a business acquisition in FY2025 and USD 1 million in the first nine months of 2026, raised USD 45 million in FY2025 from sales of property and equipment, primarily sale-leaseback of owned ATM units, divested a non-core business for USD 11 million, received USD 31.5 million from a litigation settlement in Q3 2026 and paid Voyix USD 24 million on 2026-07-17 for its half of the Hoak settlement. The USD 200 million share repurchase program approved on 2025-07-25 was used for USD 28 million in FY2025 and USD 15 million in Q1 2026 and then suspended.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Each row recomputes a figure used elsewhere in this answer from the printed inputs. Amounts are USD millions unless a unit is shown.

fields.value: Each line states what is missing, for which analysis, how serious it is and what would close it. Three are Medium and five are Low, and all are unresolved.

It restricts: Ownership change, event risk and the change-of-control conclusion. Severity Medium. To close: Obtain the merger agreement, the joint proxy statement and any acquirer financing announcements. Status: Unresolved.

It restricts: Control, governance and sponsor-risk conclusions. Severity Medium. To close: Obtain the 2026 proxy statement. Status: Unresolved.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The tax matters, separation and commercial agreements with Voyix are described only in summaries, and Voyix revenue and cost amounts inside Other revenue and cost lines are not separately disclosed. It restricts: Voyix legacy exposure and related-party leakage assessment. Severity Medium. To close: Obtain the agreements and a breakdown of Voyix flows. Status: Unresolved.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Customer renewal rates and churn, the split of remaining performance obligations by segment and product, ATM counts by ownership model and transaction volumes are not supplied. It restricts: Revenue durability and operating-model conclusions. Severity Low. To close: Obtain renewal, backlog and unit disclosure. Status: Unresolved.

fields.value: - The size of 2026 tariff refunds inside Self-Service Banking Adjusted EBITDA is not stated. It restricts: Quality of the 2026 margin gain. Severity Low. To close: Obtain the refund amounts by quarter. Status: Unresolved.

fields.value: - The credit agreement and indenture are not supplied, so events of default, restricted payment and investment capacity and any unrestricted subsidiary or priming capacity cannot be tested. It restricts: Legal-capacity link for sponsor and liability-management behavior. Severity Low. To close: Obtain the executed credit agreement, indenture and any intercreditor terms. Status: Unresolved.

fields.value: - No agency rating or market-implied view is supplied. It restricts: Event-risk calibration for the merger. Severity Low. To close: Obtain current ratings and outlooks. Status: Unresolved.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: NCR Atleos Corp (issuer id natl-1974138), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. This module synthesizes the issuer's fundamental credit profile from the eight supplied filings and releases and the three earlier answers. It assigns no rating and makes no security recommendation, legal-capacity conclusion or sizing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: NCR Atleos has an adequate credit profile that is improving on earnings and debt reduction, but a flat revenue base, a heavy 2028 and 2029 maturity wall and a change of control with undisclosed financing make event and refinancing risk the main concerns. Net debt fell to USD 2,233 million at 2026-09-30, or 2.59x on derived reported EBITDA and 2.47x on the issuer's adjusted measure for the trailing year, from 3.50x and 3.21x at 2024-12-31, although the pro forma effect of the consent fee on the 2029 secured notes is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D1; calculation D2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity of USD 882 million covers scheduled principal through 2027 about five times, so a liquidity squeeze is unlikely before 2028, but USD 2,619 million of the USD 2,792 million of principal at year-end 2025 falls due in 2028 and 2029, and FY2025 interest cover was a modest 2.75x on derived reported EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 170; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 138; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D4; calculation D5; calculation D12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business profile is average and the earnings base is steadier than it is growing. Revenue was USD 4,354 million in FY2025 and USD 4,397 million for the twelve months to 2026-09-30, 70.6% of FY2025 revenue was recurring, no customer exceeds 10% of revenue and 55% of revenue is earned outside the United States, which gives lenders visible cash flow, but recurring revenue fell 1.6% in FY2025 and rose only 0.7% in nine months of 2026 while remaining contracted revenue fell to about USD 1.8 billion from USD 2.3 billion at 2026-03-31. Self-Service Banking and Network together are 95.3% of revenue and 97.3% of segment Adjusted EBITDA, so softness in either segment reaches EBITDA directly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 165; 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; calculation D7; calculation D19; calculation D23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Deleveraging is real and has come from earnings and repayment, not from asset sales or equity. Net debt fell by USD 288 million between 2024-12-31 and 2026-09-30, trailing Adjusted EBITDA rose 8.8% to USD 903 million against FY2025, and Adjusted EBITDA margin widened from 17.6% in FY2023 to 20.5% for the trailing year, so leverage fell while debt was repaid and cash was drawn down; pro forma net debt for the consent fee on the 2029 secured notes is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D3; calculation D6; calculation D21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Part of the margin gain is unlikely to repeat. The issuer's trailing figures include net tariff refunds of unstated size, a USD 31.5 million legal settlement that lifts reported EBITDA, and a first-half benefit from lower vault cash costs, and without the legal settlement net leverage at 2026-09-30 would be 2.69x on reported EBITDA rather than 2.59x; fuel and memory chip costs are elevated and expected to stay so.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash conversion is thin, so debt reduction from internal cash flow cannot cover the maturity wall. Free cash flow was USD 200 million in FY2025 and USD 276 million for the trailing year, 24.1% and 30.6% of Adjusted EBITDA, and trailing free cash flow is only 10.8% of gross debt, or 9.2 years of repayment, because interest, taxes, capital spending including software and legacy payments absorb most of EBITDA. Capital intensity is rising with owned ATMs under ATMaaS contracts, to 4.2% of revenue in nine months of 2026 from 3.6% in FY2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 105; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 106; calculation D8; calculation D9; calculation D23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate for the next two years and the covenant test cannot be assessed here. Liquidity of USD 882 million is USD 311 million of cash and USD 571 million of undrawn revolver, against USD 80 million of principal due in 2026 and USD 93 million in 2027, a cover of 5.1x, and the revolver was undrawn at 2026-09-30; a leverage covenant is stated in the credit agreement but the covenant ratio and compliance are not supplied, so headroom is not calculated. Pro forma net debt and cash for the consent fee are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 168; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 170; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Refinancing is the central test, and the debt market currently supports it. USD 2,619 million of principal, 93.8% of the year-end 2025 total, falls due in 2028 and 2029, when the term loans A and the revolver mature on 2028-10-16, the term loan B on 2029-04-16 and the 2029 secured notes on 2029-04-01; the long-term debt had a fair value of USD 2,684 million against principal of USD 2,575 million at 2026-09-30, 104.2% of principal, and the notes are callable at a premium that steps down each year. Brink's financing and the treatment of the credit facilities at closing are not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 166; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 167; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 169; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 170; 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation D4; calculation D15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rate and cost sensitivity is material to a business with this cash conversion. The issuer estimates that a 100 bp rise in variable rates would add USD 17 million to interest expense and USD 39 million to vault cash rental cost at FY2025 volumes, USD 56 million in all, which is 6.7% of Adjusted EBITDA and 20.3% of trailing free cash flow, and the interest rate swaps on the term loans were terminated on 2025-02-18; fixed-rate notes are 52.4% of principal.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 118; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 119; 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation D16; calculation D17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy and governance are supportive in conduct and uncertain in outcome. There is no sponsor and no common dividend, buybacks of USD 43 million were suspended for the merger and debt was repaid, but a revenue-control weakness led to revised statements, Voyix legacy claims have no stated cap, and the Brink's merger, with a USD 145 million termination fee equal to 16.4% of liquidity, will change the owner and may change the debt structure on terms creditors cannot yet see.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case against an adequate, improving profile is that the improvement has run ahead of the business. Recurring revenue is flat, remaining contracted revenue has fallen for two quarters to below its FY2024 level, hardware revenue fell 20% in Q3 2026, Network managed units are shrinking and 2026 earnings include items that will not repeat, so trailing leverage of 2.47x may flatter the position, before any pro forma effect of the consent fee, which is not established; if Adjusted EBITDA slipped back to its FY2024 level with net debt unchanged, net leverage would be 2.84x, and at the FY2023 level 3.03x, still below the 3.21x of 2024-12-31 because debt has fallen. Interest is also a larger drain than leverage suggests, since interest expense absorbed 32.5% of Adjusted EBITDA in FY2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation D1; calculation D13; calculation D10; calculation D23; calculation D24

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case for a better view is that lenders already price the debt above principal, liquidity covers the two nearest years of maturities 5.1x, and Brink's may refinance the 2028 and 2029 maturities on its own terms. Publication of the acquirer's financing that repays or refinances the credit facilities, a Q4 2026 revenue recovery with remaining contracted revenue above USD 1.8 billion, or a refinancing of the 2028 maturities before closing would strengthen the view. A revolver draw to pay the consent fee, a failed merger that triggers the termination fee, remaining contracted revenue below USD 1.8 billion, or trailing Adjusted EBITDA below USD 903 million would weaken it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-03-31_natl-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; calculation D15; calculation D20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No agency rating, bond price series or peer set is supplied, so the adequate rating of the profile is judged against the issuer's own history and the competitors it names, and it would move if rated peers with similar cash conversion and maturity walls were compared.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The issuer gives no outlook and holds no earnings call while the merger is pending, so the outlook and the downside case rest on reversals of reported gains and on stated sensitivities, not on a forecast, and cannot say how far hardware and Network volumes will fall.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The credit agreement, its EBITDA definition and any compliance statement are not supplied, so the stated leverage covenant is not tested against the issuer's figures and covenant risk is left unassessed, which could change the liquidity finding if headroom is narrow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The rate sensitivities are the issuer's FY2025 estimates at FY2025 volumes and hedges, and the term loan swaps have since been terminated, so the 2026 sensitivity to rates could differ and the combined USD 56 million figure is only a guide to scale.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first credit strength is deleveraging from earnings and repayment. Net debt fell by USD 288 million in nine months to 2026-09-30 and net leverage on reported EBITDA fell to 2.59x from 3.50x, which shrinks the amount to be refinanced in 2028 and 2029 and improves the odds that lenders and an acquirer will refinance it; pro forma net debt for the consent fee is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D2; calculation D3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second strength is liquidity that outlasts the nearest maturities. Cash of USD 311 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 571 million give USD 882 million, 5.1x the USD 173 million of principal due in 2026 and 2027, so debt service does not depend on market access before 2028; pro forma cash for the consent fee is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 170; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third strength is a recurring, customer-spread revenue base. Recurring revenue was 70.6% of FY2025 revenue, no customer exceeds 10% of revenue and 55% is earned outside the United States, which limits the loss from any one customer or market and gives visibility on a large part of EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fourth strength is margin gain from ATMaaS and software. Adjusted EBITDA margin widened from 17.6% in FY2023 to 20.5% for the trailing year as services and software grew, so more EBITDA is earned on flat revenue, although part of the 2026 gain is not repeatable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fifth strength is supportive financial policy with no sponsor. The statements show no common dividend and the USD 200 million repurchase program was suspended after USD 43 million of use, so cash has gone to debt reduction, not to owners.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first credit weakness is the maturity wall. USD 2,619 million, 93.8% of year-end 2025 principal, falls due in 2028 and 2029, and trailing free cash flow of USD 276 million could repay only a small part by then, so the credit depends on refinancing in a market the sources do not show for 2028.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 170; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D4; calculation D9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second weakness is a change of control with undisclosed financing. The credit facilities make a change of control an event of default, the noteholders' waiver depends on a consent fee that is not stated, and the USD 145 million termination fee equals 16.4% of liquidity, so the owner and the debt structure may change on terms creditors cannot yet see.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 168; calculation D20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third weakness is weak revenue momentum. Recurring revenue is flat, remaining contracted revenue fell 21.7% from 2026-03-31 to 2026-09-30, Network managed units fell 4.8% in a year and hardware fell 20% in Q3 2026, so EBITDA gains must come from cost and mix while the volume base is not growing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation D23; calculation D24

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fourth weakness is thin cash conversion. Free cash flow was 24.1% of Adjusted EBITDA in FY2025 and 30.6% in the trailing year, and capital intensity is rising with owned ATMs, so each dollar of EBITDA gain adds little to debt reduction capacity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation D8; calculation D23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fifth weakness is sensitivity to rates and legacy claims. A 100 bp rise in variable rates costs about USD 56 million a year at FY2025 volumes, 6.7% of Adjusted EBITDA, and Voyix legacy indemnities and environmental claims draw cash without a stated cap.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 118; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 119; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation D16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer is a global ATM technology, services and network business, and its model gives lenders visible cash flow rather than growth. It sells ATM hardware, software, maintenance and ATM as a Service to banks and retailers, runs the Allpoint surcharge-free network and bank branding for banks and fintechs, and provides managed network services to enterprises; 70.6% of FY2025 revenue was recurring and no customer exceeds 10% of revenue, which supports debt service as long as contracts renew, but renewal rates and contract terms are not supplied and Self-Service Banking and Network are 97.3% of segment Adjusted EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 164; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 165; calculation D19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership adds no sponsor risk and adds event risk. NCR Voyix distributed all shares in 2023 and holds none, there is no sponsor or controlling shareholder in the record, and Brink's, which the annual report names as a competitor, will own the issuer outright after the two-step merger expected in early January 2027, so the party that sets financial policy is about to change while its financing is not described.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 127; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_ex-991ncratleosearningsrel.htm.jsonl, page 1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is predictable in its recurring part, cyclical in hardware, volume-sensitive in Network and mixed in direction. Hardware was 29.9% of Self-Service Banking revenue in FY2025 and fell 20% in Q3 2026, Network revenue is 97.5% transactional, and consolidated revenue growth slowed from 7% in Q1 2026 to flat in Q2 and a 2% fall in Q3, so pricing power is not evident and the recurring share of 71.2% in Q3 2026 rose only because total revenue fell; ATMaaS is growing but was only 9.0% of Self-Service Banking revenue in FY2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 103; EX-99.1_2026-05-06_ex-991ncratleosearningsrel.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_ex-991ncratleosearningsrel.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_ex-991ncratleosearningsrel.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation D24

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are defensible but not insulated, because most of the cost base is the service network and the inputs move with fuel, memory chips and rates. Cost of services was 56.7% of FY2025 revenue and selling, general and administrative expense 11.8%, Adjusted EBITDA margin widened to 20.5% for the trailing year, and the issuer expects fuel and memory chip costs to stay elevated, so margin pressure under falling volume would come through service costs that do not fall with volume and through vault cash rental, which is floating-rate on about USD 4.1 billion of cash that stays off the balance sheet.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 101; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 138; 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; calculation D6; calculation D18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: EBITDA turns into free cash flow slowly, so cash available for debt reduction is limited. Free cash flow after interest, capital spending and capitalized software was USD 200 million in FY2025 and USD 276 million for the trailing year, 24.1% and 30.6% of Adjusted EBITDA, and capital spending flexes with ATMaaS growth and sale-leaseback proceeds; cash interest was USD 268 million in FY2025, giving 2.75x cover on reported EBITDA and 3.10x on the issuer's measure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 105; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 138; calculation D8; calculation D12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive rivalry and buyer power are the forces that matter to credit. The annual report names Fiserv, Euronet, Brink's, Hyosung and Diebold Nixdorf as competitors, buyers are banks and large national retailers on long-term contracts, suppliers include single-source component makers and contract manufacturers whose cost swings reach margins through memory chips, and usage of ATMs, fee levels and bank sponsorship requirements are risks that could reduce transaction revenue; no entrant threat is evidenced, because fintechs and neobanks are mainly customers of the Allpoint network.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Macro and regulatory factors are material to credit and are the main outside drivers of the downside. Interest rates drive vault cash cost and floating interest, tariffs and the later refund of invalid tariffs moved 2026 margins, US immigration policy cut withdrawal volumes in 2025, the war in the Middle East and conflict with Iran could disrupt supply and demand, and money transmitter and cryptocurrency licensing rules apply to the Bitcoin business.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 104; 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_ex-991ncratleosearningsrel.htm.jsonl, page 2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit strengths are deleveraging, liquidity that outlasts the nearest maturities, a recurring and customer-spread revenue base, ATMaaS-led margin gains and supportive financial policy. The weaknesses are the 2028 and 2029 maturity wall, a change of control with undisclosed financing, flat recurring revenue with a shrinking backlog and fleet, thin cash conversion and rate and legacy-claim sensitivity. The opportunities that could lift credit quality are ATMaaS conversion, growth of the Allpoint network with fintechs and possible refinancing by the acquirer, and the threats are slower hardware and Network volumes, higher rates and a failed or delayed merger.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and market position is average, because revenue of USD 4,397 million for the trailing year and a global network give shock absorption but the Network fleet is shrinking and competitors are large. Competitive advantage is average, since service reach, the Allpoint network and ATMaaS contracts may raise switching costs but renewal evidence is not supplied. Business diversification is average, with geographic spread and no customer above 10% offset by 97.3% of segment Adjusted EBITDA in two segments. Cost and capex flexibility is average, because capital intensity is rising with owned ATMs although sale-leasebacks give some room.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D7; calculation D19; calculation D23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margin stability is average, with margin gains that include non-repeating items and floating-rate vault cash costs, and free cash flow stability is average because free cash flow of USD 200 million to USD 276 million is positive but is only a quarter to a third of Adjusted EBITDA and is swung by settlement timing. Ability to refinance and access capital markets is average, held back by the 2028 and 2029 maturity wall and the undisclosed merger financing but helped by debt trading above principal. Liquidity position is strong against the next two years, at 5.1x scheduled principal. Financial policy and governance is average, because policy is supportive but reporting controls were revised and Voyix claims and the merger are open.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation D4; calculation D5; calculation D8; calculation D15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months the credit depends on the merger and on the margin holding. The closing expected in early January 2027 decides who owns and finances the issuer, scheduled principal is only USD 80 million in 2026 and USD 93 million in 2027, remaining contracted revenue and hardware demand will show whether buyers are waiting for the merger, and tariff refunds and the first-half vault cash benefit may drop out of the comparison; the issuer gives no outlook, so the direction rests on reported trends.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-04_ex-991ncratleosearningsrel.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 170; 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_ex-991ncratleosearningsrel.htm.jsonl, page 3; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years the 2028 and 2029 maturities, USD 2,619 million at year-end 2025 and somewhat less after 2026 repayments, ATMaaS conversion and the cash-usage trend decide credit quality. ATMaaS and software growth and Allpoint fintech business are tailwinds, while ATM usage, transaction fees, US withdrawal policy, Bitcoin volumes and rates are headwinds, and the debt can be refinanced only if EBITDA holds and the acquirer's plan is workable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The downside is a volume and cost squeeze during the merger wait that leaves the 2028 and 2029 maturities to be refinanced from a lower EBITDA. Buyers keep delaying hardware purchases and Network volumes keep falling, which cuts Self-Service Banking and Network earnings that are 97.3% of segment Adjusted EBITDA; fuel, memory chip and vault cash costs rise and a 100 bp rise in rates adds about USD 56 million; free cash flow, now 10.8% of debt, falls below the USD 276 million trailing level; if Adjusted EBITDA returned to its FY2024 level of USD 785 million, net leverage would be 2.84x and 3.03x at the FY2023 level.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-11-04_ex-991ncratleosearningsrel.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation D9; calculation D13; calculation D16; calculation D19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity would still carry the issuer through 2027, so distress is not the base risk. Liquidity of USD 882 million is 5.1x the scheduled principal of 2026 and 2027, the revolver is undrawn, management can suspend buybacks, which it has done, slow capital spending on owned ATMs and use sale-leasebacks, and the interim merger covenants restrict new indebtedness before closing; the breaking point is refinancing the 2028 and 2029 maturities, USD 2,619 million at year-end 2025, and a failed merger that triggers the USD 145 million termination fee. Pro forma net debt for the consent fee is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_natl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 170; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation D5; calculation D20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, NCR Atleos presents an adequate business profile supported by recurring revenue, customer and geographic spread and ATMaaS-led margin gains, but credit quality is constrained by a flat revenue base, thin cash conversion and a maturity wall of USD 2,619 million in 2028 and 2029 at year-end 2025. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow is positive and liquidity covers the next two years, though only 30.6% of Adjusted EBITDA converts to free cash flow. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on market access, which currently prices the debt above principal, and on how Brink's finances the combination. The primary downside path is a fall in hardware and Network volumes during the merger wait that cuts the EBITDA needed to refinance in 2028 and 2029. Further analysis would require the merger agreement and acquirer financing, the credit agreement and covenant compliance, renewal data and ratings. Top risk: refinancing the 2028 and 2029 maturities while the change of control and its financing are unresolved.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ncr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 170; calculation D4; calculation D8; calculation D15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Each row recomputes a figure used elsewhere in this answer from the stated inputs, or restates a figure from an earlier answer. Amounts are USD millions unless a unit is shown.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Each line states what is missing, which conclusion it restricts, how serious it is and what would close it. Two are Medium and four are Low, and all are unresolved.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The treatment of the credit facilities at closing, the consent fee amount and the acquirer's financing are not stated, so the post-closing debt structure and pro forma net debt are not established. It restricts: the refinancing view and the event-risk ranking. Severity Medium. To close: merger agreement and acquirer financing documents. Status: Unresolved.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No agency rating, bond price series or peer set is supplied. It restricts: the comparison of this profile with rated peers and the market's view of event risk. Severity Medium. To close: current ratings, bond prices and a peer set. Status: Unresolved.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Renewal rates, contract terms and the split of contracted revenue by segment are not supplied. It restricts: the revenue durability and backlog conclusions. Severity Low. To close: contract and backlog disclosure by segment. Status: Unresolved.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The credit agreement, its EBITDA definition and the covenant compliance statement are not supplied. It restricts: the liquidity and leverage conclusions where a covenant could bind. Severity Low. To close: credit agreement and compliance certificate. Status: Unresolved.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The size of 2026 tariff refunds and of Voyix amounts inside revenue and cost lines is not stated. It restricts: the repeatability of the 2026 margin gain. Severity Low. To close: quarterly refund and Voyix flow schedules. Status: Unresolved.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The debt maturity ladder is printed only at 2025-12-31, so principal repaid in 2026 is not scheduled and the wall at 2026-09-30 is not shown. It restricts: the size of the 2028 and 2029 maturities. Severity Low. To close: a ladder at 2026-09-30 or tranche balances. Status: Unresolved.
